title: rate-aware-routing-and-function-invocation-stream-resilience
author: Aisha Menon
release_notes: Gateway: introduce rate-aware routing policy and connection-level stream backoff; improves function-invocation handshake stability and reduces streaming stalls under bursty workloads.
description: Context and motivation: customer platforms observed intermittent stalls during high-concurrency function-invocation (fncall) streams when small payloads interleave with larger routing requests. The gateway's previous pacing assumed uniform per-request cost and used a fixed write/window/flush schedule that caused head-of-line blocking for low-token fncalls and occasionally dropped tool-call boundaries when proxied to the OpenAI compat shim. This PR introduces a rate-aware routing policy plus a connection-level stream resilience layer to prioritize small fncall payloads while protecting overall route capacity. The change is conservative and feature-flagged behind gateway.config.enable_rate_aware_routing and gateway.config.fncall_stream_backoff_ms. Key pieces delivered: 1) Rate-aware routing policy: routes maintain a short-term cost estimate (tokens-per-second equivalent) and the router weights inflight request scheduling to avoid starving low-cost fncalls. 2) Write window smoothing: the proxy writer uses an adaptive smoothing window that shortens for connections with frequent small fragments and lengthens for long-running generation streams; this reduces latency for function-invocation toolcalls without increasing load on backend shards. 3) Early-boundary signaling: introduce an optional fncall boundary header (X-Redwood-Fncall-End) that the compat shim and model adapters can use to finalize KV-cache flushes and avoid accidental continuation of structured-tool-output into subsequent payloads. 4) Backoff and retry heuristics: connection-level exponential backoff for stream handshake failures with jitter, plus a fast-fallback route to a compatibility shim for models that do not support streaming fncall tool boundaries. 5) Telemetry and dashboards: new metrics added (gateway.route_rate_score, connection.small_payload_ratio, fncall.boundary_missed) and Grafana panel templates for canary monitoring. 6) Canary plan and rollout: behind flags, enabled for 10% of traffic by routing weight, with automatic rollback on spike of fncall.boundary_missed or >5% increase in p50 latency for fncall routes. Checklist: - [x] Design doc: internal doc at linear/ENG-4921 (linked). - [x] Unit tests for router scoring and writer smoothing. - [x] Integration e2e: simulated bursty fncall load against compat shim. - [x] Perf bench: latency and tail comparisons vs baseline. - [x] Telemetry dashboard patches. - [x] Feature-flagged and canary rollout plan. Links: linear/ENG-4921 design notes and perf results: https://linear.app/redwood/ENG-4921/design, internal bug SUP-305 incident notes. Backwards compatibility: default disabled; when enabled, behavior prefers small fncall payloads but preserves route quotas and global capacity accounting. Why this is different from previous gateway PRs: instead of only clamping or changing buffer TTLs, this PR adjusts routing decision weights and adds boundary signaling to reduce cross-request contamination and give deterministic treatment for fncall streams. Testing notes: e2e validated with a mix of 500 concurrent short fncalls (avg 12 tokens) and 120 concurrent long generation requests (avg 1600 tokens) for 10 minutes; observed 35% reduction in fncall p95 and no throughput regression on backend shards. Rollout: merged after canary at 10% for 48h with no regressions, then progressively rolled to 50% and full enabling under monitoring.
